content.text: I fixed the bug in `solution/core.py`, and the visible suite now passes (2 passed). When the loop merged an interval into the last one in the output, it replaced the end with the new interval's end, `out[-1] = (pa, b)`. Intervals are sorted only by start, so a later interval can end before the previous one. That happens when it sits inside it, like `(2, 3)` within `(1, 4)` or the point `(2, 2)` within `(1, 3)`, and the merged interval got cut short. The fix keeps whichever end is larger: `out[-1] = (pa, max(pb, b))`. The bug wasn't tied to `join_touching=False`; the same truncation happened with `join_touching=True`, and the fix covers both. I also checked a few cases by hand. Containment merges correctly with either setting, as does a chain like `[(1,5),(2,3),(4,6)]` → `[(1,6)]`. With `join_touching=False`, touching intervals still stay separate (`[(1,3),(3,5)]`) and duplicate points still collapse to one.

When the loop merged an interval into the last one in the output, it replaced the end with the new interval's end, `out[-1] = (pa, b)`. Intervals are sorted only by start, so a later interval can end before the previous one. That happens when it sits inside it, like `(2, 3)` within `(1, 4)` or the point `(2, 2)` within `(1, 3)`, and the merged interval got cut short. The fix keeps whichever end is larger: `out[-1] = (pa, max(pb, b))`. The bug wasn't tied to `join_touching=False`; the same truncation happened with `join_touching=True`, and the fix covers both. I also checked a few cases by hand. Containment merges correctly with either setting, as does a chain like `[(1,5),(2,3),(4,6)]` → `[(1,6)]`. With `join_touching=False`, touching intervals still stay separate (`[(1,3),(3,5)]`) and duplicate points still collapse to one.
